R package: analysis framework

An R analysis framework built for AI agents.

One layout, rules that code enforces, and fake data with known answers. An AI agent checks its own code with pbn::verify(), and each problem comes with its fix.

Get started pbn with AI agents

pbn

An R analysis framework built for AI agents.

pbn (“paint by numbers”) is for analysis projects where an AI agent writes code. The agent checks its own code with pbn::verify(). Each finding of a rule names its fix. pbn gives each project one layout and rules that code enforces. The fake scenarios have expected values. They run through the same code as the real data. A person confirms the expected values.

What pbn does

  • One way to do each thing. One run script, up to four data steps, and pbn::folder() for every path to the data.
  • Checks that name the fix. pbn::check_project() checks the project folder against the rules in pbn.yml. Checks between the data steps stop a run that breaks their contract, for example a step clean that drops rows. Each finding names the rule, the file and the fix.
  • Verification on fake data. The real data is one scenario among fake ones with expected values. expect_ functions check each fake scenario, and pbn::read_results() does not read the results of a fake scenario with a failed assertion. It also does not read the real results of a run that had a fake scenario with a failed assertion.
  • Records to review. Each run writes check.csv with every assertion, a run log run.md, and a manifest with the md5 of the code. A person reviews these files as well as the changed lines.
  • An agent needs no real data. It works on the code and the fake scenarios. pbn::to_one_file() writes the code for the run of the real data into one script, for a server without a network.

pbn is the only package of its family that sets rules for a project. org (paths), cohort (exclusions) and plnr (plans) set no rules.

For an AI agent

Read https://www.rwhite.no/pbn/articles/pbn.md before you write or change the run script of an analysis project. It is the manual of pbn as one worked example, in plain Markdown, written for an agent to read as one file. https://www.rwhite.no/pbn/llms.txt lists every other page. pbn::create_project() writes AGENTS.md from the template inst/templates/AGENTS.md. It lists what to run before a report, and what a person decides.

Installation 

pak::pak("raubreywhite/pbn")

Quick start

In an empty folder:

pbn::create_project(folders = c(main = "../data"))
pbn::verify("v01")

create_project() writes a project at version v01 that passes pbn::check_project(). Its run script runs the fake scenarios only, so pbn::verify("v01") gives a PASS before code reads the real data. It stops, and writes nothing, when one of its files exists. pbn::new_version("v01") freezes v01 and starts v02.

Start a new project with an agent

Copy this prompt to the agent. Fill in the folder and the study:

Set up a new R analysis project with the R package pbn, in this folder.
1. Read https://www.rwhite.no/pbn/articles/pbn.md, the manual of pbn.
2. If pbn and cohort are not installed, install them with pak::pak(c("raubreywhite/pbn", "raubreywhite/cohort")).
3. Run pbn::create_project(folders = c(main = "<folder of the real data>")).
4. Do not open, copy or print the real data.
5. The study: <question, population, exposure, outcome>.
6. Replace the scenario `known`, `expect_known()` and `fit_risk_difference()` of the project with ones for this study. Write the data steps and the analyses. Write fake scenarios with expected values: one small scenario whose values a person can compute by hand, and for each estimate one fake scenario with many simulations (`sims`).
7. Keep `only` in the call `pbn::scenarios()` of v01_run.R until a person runs the real data.
8. Run pbn::verify("v01") until the verdict is PASS.
9. Then stop. List each fake scenario and its expected values, and wait for me to confirm them.
